Analyzing pi-ui-server-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, pointing to prebuilt `.tar.zst` archives hosted on GitHub under the maintainer's repository (https://github.com/hyperpuncher/pi-ui). The URLs are constructed using the declared `pkgver`, which is a static string (`0.33.0`) and not dynamically computed via command substitution or external calls. There is no `pkgver()` function present, so no dynamic version fetching occurs.

The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments. No command substitutions (e.g., `$(...)` or backticks), function calls, or executable statements are present outside of the `package()` function — which will not be executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags. The `source`, `sha256sums`, and architecture-specific variants are all properly declared and point to verifiable, static upstream release artifacts.

Fetching these sources using `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will download the specified tarballs and the LICENSE file. While the checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', even if they were, that would not make this step unsafe — as extraction without execution is safe under these flags. No code is executed during sourcing, and no network requests occur outside of the declared sources.
</details>
<summary>
No execution during source fetch; all safe.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No execution during source fetch; all safe.

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries from the project's official GitHub repository (https://github.com/hyperpuncher/pi-ui) for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The source URLs point directly to release binaries under the declared upstream, which is consistent with standard packaging practices for binary distributions. Each architecture-specific binary has a corresponding SHA-256 checksum that matches the file being downloaded, ensuring integrity. The package installs only two files: the binary to `/usr/bin/pi-ui-server` and the LICENSE file to the standard licensing directory.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, suspicious network activity, or unauthorized file operations. The use of `!strip` in options is noted but justified for binary packages where symbol stripping may interfere with debugging or expected operation. No `eval`, `curl|bash`, or other dangerous patterns are present. The maintainer provides correct and verifiable sources with proper checksums, and all operations occur within the build environment without side effects. While the binaries are prebuilt and thus not auditable here, the packaging itself follows safe and transparent practices.

The package conflicts with `pi-ui-server` and provides `pi-ui-server=$pkgver`, which helps prevent version clashes—this is good packaging hygiene. No post-install hooks or system modifications are performed. Everything in the PKGBUILD serves the legitimate purpose of installing a binary release securely and predictably.
</details>
<summary>
Safe binary package with verified checksums from official source</summary>
</security_assessment>
